Rashi on Shabbat 63b:10:1.hebrew: ושלשלת משוי להו מנא - בתמיה, דקתני כבלים טמאים:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:10:1.english: And does a chain make them into a vessel? - [This is asked] in astonishment, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "[Ankle] chains are susceptible to ritual impurity."

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:11:1.english: And if you say, in accordance with Rabbi Shmuel, etc.:

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:11:2.english: [That which] makes a sound with metal vessels - [This was explained] at the beginning of our chapter.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:13:1.hebrew: ועשו להן שלשלת כו' - הלכך, שלשלת תשמיש אדם הוא, ולאו תשמיש כלי — דלא תקבל טומאה. ואין יוצאין בהן — דילמא שלפא לשלשלת, שהיא של זהב, ומחויא; דכי שקלת לשלשלת, לא מיגליא שוקה, שהרי בירית במקומה עומדת:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:13:1.english: And they made them a chain, etc. - Therefore, the chain is [an object of] human use, and not [merely] an accessory of an implement, which would not contract ritual impurity. And [as for why] they may not go out in them [on Shabbat — it is] lest she remove the chain, which is [made] of gold, and show [it]; for when she takes off the chain, her leg is not exposed, as the garter remains in its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:13:2.hebrew: יישר וכן אמר ר' יוחנן - יפה אמרת, וכן שמעתי מר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:13:2.english: Correct, and Rabbi Yoḥanan said likewise - You have spoken well, and so I heard from Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:14:1.english: From the frontplate [tzitz] - For it is a small item, and [Scripture] counted it among the ornaments of the [High] Priest.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:15:1.hebrew: יו"ד ה"א מלמעלה קדש למ"ד מלמטה - כלומר, השם שלם בשיטה עליונה, וקדש למ"ד בשיטה תחתונה, שלא להקדים שאר אותיות למעלה מן השם, מאחר ששני שיטין היו. ורבינו הלוי שונה: ״קודש לה' מלמטה״, והיא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:15:1.english: Yod heh above, kodesh lamed below - That is to say, the [Divine] Name in its entirety [was written] on the upper line, and “kodesh lamed” on the lower line, so as not to place other letters above the [Divine] Name, since there were two lines. And Rabbeinu HaLevi recites: “Kodesh laHashem below,” and it is one and the same.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:16:1.hebrew: אני ראיתיו ברומי - שנכנס לאוצר המלך ליטול מה שירצה, במס' מעילה (דף טו:) במעשה בן תלמיון:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:16:1.english: I saw it in Rome - For he entered the king’s treasury to take whatever he wished, [as related] in tractate Me'ilah (15b) in the incident of Ben Telamyon.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:17:1.hebrew: כי סליק רב דימי לנהרדעא - חזר בו ממה שאמר: ציץ אריג הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:17:1.english: When Rav Dimi ascended to Neharde’a - He retracted what he had said, [namely, that] the frontplate is a woven fabric.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:17:2.hebrew: מאו בגד - דכתיב גבי שרצים: "או בגד או עור" — "או" ריבוי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:17:2.english: From “Or a garment” - For it is written regarding creeping animals: “Or a garment, or skin” — “or” is an inclusion.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:18:1.hebrew: אריג ותכשיט כל שהוא - חציו אריג וחציו תכשיט שאינו אריג, וכולו הוי כל שהוא — כלומר, דבר קטן:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:18:1.english: Woven fabric and an ornament of any size - Half of it is woven fabric and half of it is an ornament that is not woven fabric, and the whole of it is of any size — that is to say, a small object.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:18:2.hebrew: מוסיף שק על הבגד - בדבר זה — שהשק טמא משום אריג. ולקמיה מפרש ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:18:2.english: A sack is added to a garment - In this matter: that a sack is ritually impure due to [being considered] woven fabric. And further on, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:1:1.hebrew: מרעהו - מונע חסד. ואע"ג דלא כתיב מונע, ממילא משמע, שכל תיבה שראשה מ"ם משמשת נטילה היא, כמו: ויקח מידם (שמות ל״ב:ד׳), אבדו גוים מארצו (תהילים י׳:ט״ז):
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:1:1.english: From his friend - [This means] withholding kindness. And even though [the word] “withholds” is not written, it is understood implicitly, for every word whose beginning is a mem serves [to denote] removal, as in: “And he took from their hand” (Exodus 32:4), [and] “The nations have perished from His land” (Psalms 10:16).

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:20:1.hebrew: ההוא במדין כתיב - גבי טומאת מת, ושרץ ממת לא יליף להחמיר — דמה למת, שכן טומאתו חמורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:20:1.english: That is written with regard to Midian - Regarding the ritual impurity of a corpse; and [the impurity of] a creeping animal is not derived from a corpse to be stringent, for what [comparison can be made] to a corpse, as its impurity is severe?

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:1.hebrew: למיפא - לאפות עיסה, שהשאיל בעה"ב תנורו:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:1.english: To bake - To bake dough, as the homeowner had lent his oven.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:2.hebrew: שקילי ניביה - נטולות ד' שיניו שהוא נושך בהן. אותן שיניים קרי ניבין, כדאמרינן באלו טרפות (חולין דף נט.): גמל ניבי אית ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:2.english: His teeth have been removed - Removed are its four teeth with which it bites. Those teeth are called nivein, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 59a): “A camel has canines.”

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:3.english: His claws have been removed - His claws have been removed [preventing him] from scratching.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:4.english: Taken - Your favor is taken and cast upon the thorns.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:5.hebrew: טיבותיך - טובת הנאת נחמתך, כמו מחזיק טוב, הגרי"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:2:5.english: Your goodness - The favor of the benefit of your consolation, as in [the expression] “acknowledging a favor” — gred [a favor] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:3:1.english: Until here - Up to: “And know that for all these...”

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:4:1.hebrew: עד כאן לתורה - שמח בתלמודך, למוד משמחה ומטוב לב, והלך בדרכי לבך — להבין מה בלבך לפי ראות עיניך:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:4:1.english: Until here, [it refers] to Torah - Rejoice in your study; study out of joy and gladness of heart; and “walk in the ways of your heart” — to understand what is in your heart, according to the sight of your eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:4:2.hebrew: מכאן ואילך למעשים טובים - "ודע כי על כל אלה" — על כל מה שלמדת, סופך ליתן את הדין, אם לא תקיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:4:2.english: From here on, [it refers] to good deeds - “And know that for all these” — for all that you have learned, you will ultimately face judgment if you do not fulfill [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:5:1.english: An armlet - [An ornament] of the arm.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:6:1.hebrew: ואילו אצעדה טמאה היא - דכתיב (במדבר לא) במעשה מדין: "אצעדה וצמיד" וגו', וכתיב: "תתחטאו אתם ושביכם":
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:6:1.english: Whereas an armlet is ritually impure - For it is written (Numbers 31) in the episode of Midian: “Armlet and bracelet…” and it is written: “Purify yourselves, you and your captives.”

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:7:1.hebrew: תחת אצעדה - שבזרוע — עומדת בשוק, להחזיק בתי שוקיה, שלא יפלו ויראו שוקיה. הלכך, טהורה — דלאו לנוי היא, וכלי תשמיש נמי לא הוי, אלא כלי המשמש כלי, דומיא דטבעות הכלים, דאמרינן בפרקין דלעיל דטהורין. ויוצאין בהם — דצורך לבישה היא, ומישלף ואחויי נמי ליכא למיחש — דלא מיגליא לשוקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 63b:7:1.english: In place of a bracelet - [Which is worn] on the arm — [the garter] is placed on the leg to hold up her stockings, so that they do not fall and her legs be exposed. Therefore, [it] is pure, because it is not for ornament, nor is it a utilitarian implement, but rather an implement that serves an implement, similar to the rings of utensils, of which we said earlier in our chapter that they are pure. And one may go out with them [on Shabbat], as it is a necessity of dressing; and there is also no concern of [her] removing and showing [it], for she will not expose her leg.

Rashi on Shabbat 63b:8:1.english: A garter on one - [On one] of her legs.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:14:1.hebrew: מניין לאריג כל שהוא שהוא טמא ת"ל או בגד - וא"ת: והא לעיל בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כו. ושם) לא מרבינן אלא ג' על ג'? וי"ל: דהתם מיירי בבא מבגד גדול, אבל הכא מיירי באריג כל שהוא דמתחלה לא היה דעתו להוסיף עליו. ותרוייהו שמעינן מאו בגד, דשקולים הם — דחשיב כל שהוא אריג מתחלה כמו ג' על ג' מבגד גדול. וא"ת: ואכתי, בגד כל שהוא למה הוא טמא? והא בעינן שיטלטל מלא וריקן דומיא דשק! וי"ל: דראוי הוא לכוף ולקפל, וליקח בו מרגלית או מחט. ואם תאמר: א"כ, פשוטי כלי עור אמאי טהורין? הרי ראויין הם לקפל בו שום דבר כמו הכא! וי"ל: דמיירי בעור שלוק, שהוא קשה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:14:1.english: From where [is it derived] that a woven fabric of any size is ritually impure? The verse states: "Or a garment" - And if you say: But earlier, in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 26a and there), we include only [a scrap measuring] three by three? And one can say: There, it is dealing with [a scrap that] came from a large garment, but here, it is dealing with a woven fabric of any size where from the start his intention was not to add to it. And both of them we derive from "or a garment," for they are equally balanced — as [a fabric of] any size that was woven from the start is considered like [a piece of] three by three [that came] from a large garment. And if you say: Still, why is a garment of any size ritually impure? But don't we require that it be moved while full and while empty, similar to a sack? And one can say: It is fit to bend and fold, and to hold a pearl or a needle in it. And if you say: If so, why are flat leather vessels ritually pure? Aren't they [also] fit to fold something inside them, like here? And one can say: It is dealing with boiled leather, which is stiff.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:15:1.hebrew: וכתוב עליו בשני שיטין יו"ד ה"א מלמעלה וקדש למ"ד למטה - נראה לר"ת שהיה כתוב יו"ד ה"א בסוף שיטה ראשונה, וקדש ל' בתחלת שיטה שניה, והשתא נקרא יפה. ואין לפרש כמשמעו, דא"כ אינו נקרא כהלכתו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:15:1.english: "And on it is written in two lines: Yod Heh above, and kodesh lamed below" - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam that Yod Heh was written at the end of the first line, and kodesh lamed at the beginning of the second line, and now it reads well. And it is not to be explained according to its literal meaning, for if so, it would not be read according to its proper order.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:17:1.hebrew: מניין לתכשיט כל שהוא טמא - ואם תאמר: תיפוק ליה דתכשיט כל שהוא טמא מדכתיב בכלי מדין "טבעת"? ויש לומר: דאפשר שהטבעת היא עבה וגדולה מאד, ולא הוי כל שהוא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:17:1.english: "From where [is it derived] that an ornament of any size is ritually impure" - And if you say: Let it be derived that an ornament of any size is ritually impure from that which is written regarding the vessels of Midian: "A ring"? And one can say: It is possible that the ring was very thick and large, and [thus] was not [merely] of any size.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:18:1.hebrew: אריג ותכשיט - פי': חציו אריג וחציו תכשיט — טמא. מכאן משמע דמ"מ בעינן שיעור קצת, דאל"כ, חציו דכ"ש מאי הוי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:18:1.english: "Woven fabric and an ornament" - Explanation: [An item that is] half woven fabric and half an ornament is impure. From here it is implied that nevertheless we require some [minimal] measure; for if not so, what would half of "any size" be?

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:20:1.hebrew: ההוא במדין כתיב - פ"ה: ובמדין הויא טומאת מת, ושרץ ממת לא יליף להחמיר, דמה למת — שכן טומאה חמורה. ומשני: "גמר כלי כלי משרץ", פירוש: מה כלי האמור בשרץ מטמא בשרץ, אף כלי האמור כאן מטמא בשרץ. וקשה: דא"כ, הוה ליה למיפרך: "ההוא בטומאת מת כתיב"! ועוד, כי משני "גמר כלי כלי", הוה ליה לשנויי: גמר "בגד" ו"עור" לג"ש! לכן נ"ל, ד"ההוא במדין כתיב" — בשלל מדין, ולא מיירי הך פרשה בטומאה כלל; והיכי יליף דאריג ותכשיט כל שהוא טמא מ"כל כלי מעשה"? ומשני: "גמר כלי כלי", פי': כי היכי דכלי דכתיב גבי שרצים מיירי לענין טומאה, הכי נמי כלי דכתיב גבי מדין — לענין טומאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:20:1.english:
"That is written with regard to Midian" - Rashi explained: And in Midian it was corpse contamination, and [impurity from] a creeping animal cannot be derived from a corpse to be stringent, for what [is true] of a corpse is that it is a severe ritual impurity. And [the Gemara] answers: He derived [via a verbal analogy of] "vessel" [and] "vessel" from [the passage of] a creeping animal. Explanation: Just as the "vessel" stated regarding a creeping animal becomes impure through a creeping animal, so too the "vessel" stated here becomes impure through a creeping animal.
And this is difficult: For if so, he should have objected: "That is written regarding corpse contamination!" Furthermore, when [the Gemara] answers: "He derived [it from] 'vessel' [and] 'vessel,'" it should have answered that he derived "garment" and "leather" as a verbal analogy!
Therefore, it seems to me that "That is written with regard to Midian" [means that it is] written regarding the spoils of Midian, and that passage does not deal with ritual impurity at all; so how could he derive that a woven fabric and an ornament of any size is ritually impure from "all vessels with which labor is done" (Numbers 31:51)? And [the Gemara] answers: "He derived [it from] 'vessel' [and] 'vessel'"; explanation: just as "vessel" written regarding creeping animals deals with the matter of ritual impurity, so too "vessel" written regarding Midian [applies] to the matter of ritual impurity.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:6:1.hebrew: ואילו אצעדה טמאה היא - פ"ה: דכתיב במעשה מדין "אצעדה וצמיד וגו'", וכתיב: "תתחטאו אתם ושביכם". ולא נהירא, דע"כ "תתחטאו" לא אכל השבי קאי, דהא בהמות נמי הוו בשבי ולאו בני קבולי טומאה נינהו. לכן נ"ל: משום דכתיב "אצעדה וצמיד", וכתיב בתריה "ויקח (מהם) כל כלי מעשה" — דקאי אכל הכלים שנלקחו, וילפינן לקמן "כלי" "כלי" משרצים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:6:1.english: "While an armlet is ritually impure" - Rashi explained that it is written in the incident of Midian: “Armlet and bracelet, etc.” (Numbers 31:50), and it is written: “Purify yourselves, you and your captives” (ibid. 31:19). But this does not seem correct, for perforce “purify yourselves” does not apply to all of the captivity, since animals were also in the captivity and they are not capable of contracting ritual impurity. Therefore, it appears to me [that the source is] because it is written: “Armlet and bracelet,” and it is written after it: “And [Moses and Elazar] took [from them] all crafted vessels” (ibid. 31:51) — which refers to all the vessels that were taken — and we derive below [via a verbal analogy of] “vessel” [and] “vessel” from [the laws of] creeping animals.

Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:7:1.hebrew: בירית תחת אצעדה עומדת - פי' בקונטרס: בשוק, להחזיק בתי שוקיה שלא יפלו ויראו שוקיה. וקשה לפי' זה: דא"כ, בכבלים אמאי אין יוצאין, למאי דס"ד השתא דאין חילוק בין בירית לכבלים אלא שזה באחת וזה בשתים? לכן נ"ל, דאפשר ליטלן בלא גילוי שוקים, ומש"ה כבלים אין יוצאין בהן — דילמא שלפא ומחויא, דתכשיט לנוי הם; אבל בירית שהיא באחת לא שלפא ומחויא, דאין זה תכשיט, דכיון שאין לה אלא באחת גנאי היא לה. ומש"ה ניחא דבירית טהורה — דלאו תכשיט לנוי הוא, וכלי תשמיש נמי לא הוי, אלא כלי המשמש כלי, דומיא דטבעת הכלי דאמר לעיל דטהור; וכן פירש הקונטרס. וטעמא דכבלים טמאים — משום דתכשיט הם לנוי, כדפי':
Tosafot on Shabbat 63b:7:1.english: A garter is in place of a bracelet - Rashi explained: [It is worn] on the leg to hold up her stockings so that they do not fall and expose her legs. But this explanation is difficult: for if so, why may [women] not go out with ankle chains, according to what [the Gemara] currently assumes, that there is no difference between a garter and ankle chains other than that this one is [worn] on one [leg] and that one is [worn] on two? Therefore, it seems to me that it is possible to remove them without exposing [one's] legs, and for that reason, [women] may not go out with ankle chains, lest she remove [them] and show [them to her friends], as they are an ornament for beauty; but with a garter, which is [worn] on one [leg], she will not remove [it] and show [it], for this is not an ornament, since having it on only one [leg] is unseemly for her. And for this reason, it works out well that a garter is ritually pure — for it is not an ornament for beauty, nor is it a functional utensil, but rather a utensil that serves [another] utensil, similar to the ring of a utensil, of which [the Gemara] said above that it is pure; and so Rashi explained. And the reason why ankle chains are ritually impure is that they are an ornament for beauty, as [I have] explained.
